newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to receive rail sell-off bids Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to receive rail sell-off bids Sept 30.

text.p: Mexico's Communications and Transport Minister Carlos Ruiz Sacristan said Wednesday the government will receive sealed bids September 30 for the Chihuahua-Pacific railroad, the first of several it plans to sell concessions for to the private sector.
"This will be next Monday," Ruiz said in a speech to Mexico's College of Civil Engineers.
Officials said the bids consisted of technical and economic proposals by the bidding firms and that a decision on the winner would be announced by October 9.
Three groups are bidding for the railroad, which runs through the spectacular Copper Canyon tourist attraction.
They are led by Mexican shipping giant Transportacion Maritima Mexicana, construction firm Tribasa and mining firm Grupo Mexico.
The railroad is one of four rail concessions the government is offering to the private sector.
Bids for the second one, covering the northeast, will be received November 29 and a decision will be announced a few days later, officials said.
